marta_cs: Hey billing team — customer reports AWS marketplace credits from a Private Offer (MPO-987654) didn't appear on their linked subaccount after activation on 2026-02-28. They've attached the invoice and the marketplace order id.
ryan_billing: Can you paste the customer's Redwood account id and the AWS account id? Usually it's an entitlement sync issue between Marketplace and our billing ledger.
alex_infra: Account mapping might be wrong — did they register under the master payer or the linked account when claiming credits? That changes the entitlements we fetch.
marta_cs: Customer account: acct-84b-7f. AWS payer account: 123456789012. They say they clicked "Activate" in AWS console and got the confirmation email.
ryan_billing: Thanks. I pulled the ledger for acct-84b-7f — no marketplace_credit entries. Could be that marketplace webhook failed or our entitlement-sync job skipped that org.
cleo-bot: Automated check: marketplace-entitlement-sync for AWS account 123456789012 completed at 2026-03-02T14:31:22Z — 0 new entitlements applied. (run-id: sync-20260302-1429)
sam_support: Customer also reported 409 on our /billing/credits/apply API when they tried to reconcile via console: ``\{"error\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"entitlement already claimed or pending\"\}``. They forwarded the confirmation email which shows activation succeeded on their side.
ryan_billing: That 409 is odd — ours returns 409 when duplicate claim attempt made. But if we never recorded it, the webhook probably hit us and errored before DB write. Need to check the webhook logs for that run-id.
alex_infra: I can grep the webhook logs. Running: ``grep \"MPO-987654\" /var/log/marketplace-webhook/*.log | tail -n 50`` — will share results.
cleo-bot: Log snippet (sanitized): ``2026-03-02T14:31:20Z INFO received_offer MPO-987654 payload_id: pl_abc123
2026-03-02T14:31:21Z ERROR entitlement-apply failed for acct-84b-7f: DBUniqueConstraintViolation (attempted write entitle_id: ent-20260302-77)``
marta_cs: Can you repro the DBUniqueConstraintViolation locally? That suggests a partially applied transaction left a tombstone. Customer sees credits missing but our DB thinks it's pending or duplicate.
ryan_billing: I'll escalate to DB ops to inspect the failed transaction id ent-20260302-77. In parallel, Alex, can you run the entitlement reconciliation for acct-84b-7f? Command: ``./scripts/reconcile_marketplace_entitlements --account acct-84b-7f --order MPO-987654``
alex_infra: Running reconcile now. Output: ``found pending ent ent-20260302-77, status: partial_write -> marking for retry``
alex_infra: After retry: ``ent-20260302-77 applied -> credit record created: credit-aws-MPO-987654-1 -> amount 5000 USD_credits``
cleo-bot: Post-reconcile sync: ledger updated for acct-84b-7f. New entry credit-aws-MPO-987654-1 timestamp 2026-03-02T14:37:55Z.
marta_cs: Customer notified. They confirmed credits now show in console. They still saw a transient 409 earlier — can we add a retry around the webhook apply path to avoid partial writes?
alex_infra: Filed infra issue: INFRA-1129 to add idempotent retries and clearer logging. Patch queued.
ryan_billing: I'll follow up with AWS Marketplace team asking for delivery guarantees and to surface webhook delivery receipts so we can reconcile automatically. Drafted message sent to aws-marketplace@partners.aws with logs and run-id.
sam_support: Closing loop with customer, left them notes and the reconciliation run id. Marking as resolved on our side but leaving INFRA-1129 open until retry logic is in prod. :thumbsup:
marta_cs: Thanks all. Saving notes to the case: MPO-987654 reconciliation, ent-20260302-77 fixed, INFRA-1129 for retries.
